presentation.method: Shown in the conversation, then the same A/B prose displayed side by side in a Funnel HTML page at the user’s request.
presentation.context: The existing conversation already contained the skill, manifest, and earlier preferences. This was a source-versus-edit comparison, not independent skill-on/skill-off generation.

samples.label: A
samples.output: This was a small, unblinded agent check with one output per case and version. It was not a no-guidance experiment, a repeated statistical comparison, or an independent human review. The five outputs within each arm shared a context. Agents were directed to read the skill files; normal runtime discovery, a new Codex session, and a Claude Code invocation were not exercised. Native-level English quality, human comprehension, reading time, token cost, and latency remain unmeasured for this revision.

samples.label: B
samples.output:
Each instruction version was checked on five cases, with one output per case. Within each version, the same agent context handled all five cases. This was a small, unblinded check. It included no comparison against unguided outputs, no repeated statistical comparison, and no independent human review.

Agents were told to read the skill files. The check therefore did not test whether the skill would be discovered and invoked through the normal workflow in a new Codex session or in Claude Code.

For this revision, native-level English quality, human comprehension, reading time, token cost, and latency remain unmeasured.
